# 1DollarPerDay: full platform reference

One block per reviewed platform, generated 2026-11-12 from the review pages at https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/. Short index: https://1dollaperday.com/llms.txt

## 2Captcha

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/2captcha
- Verdict: Gap-Filler Only, 5/10
- Category: Micro-tasks
- Status: Active, scored
- Site Type: Captcha Solving
- Min Payout: $0.50
- Payment Methods: PayPal, WebMoney, Payeer, Bitcoin, Crypto
- Hourly Rate: $0.50 to $1.00
- Earning Type: 100% Active
- Our Verdict: Legit, but use sparingly

2Captcha is legitimate and it pays. That is the good news. The bad news is that it pays $0.50 to $1.00 per hour, making it the lowest-yield method we have ever tested. It is 100% active work staring at image puzzles, nothing passive about it. Use it strictly as a gap-filler when you have dead screen time and nothing better queued. Rating: 5/10.

## 9Chain Community

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/9chain
- Verdict: No Payout Yet
- Category: Other
- Status: Unscored or unproven
- Site Type: Points farm for a blockchain project
- Cost: Free, no hardware or deposit
- Cash-Out: None described
- Referral Pay: 20% direct, 10% indirect (in points)
- Not Available In: EEA, UK, Switzerland, US
- Operator: Not named

9Chain Community is not a way to earn money today. It's a points game attached to a blockchain project: you start a "simulated" node in your browser, run quests and invite friends to collect LOVE9 Points. The site says plainly that the points are not assets, can't be transferred and can't be converted inside the app, and that any future use would need a formal proposal and community vote. It is free and asks for no deposit, but it names no operator and its points have no defined value. Spend ten minutes a day at most, and only if you're happy to farm points for a possible token that may never arrive.

## Acashly

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/acashly
- Verdict: Offline
- Category: Crypto faucets
- Status: Offline, closed or avoid
- Site Type: GPT, PTC, offerwalls, shortlinks, faucet
- Minimum Withdrawal: $1.00 (claimed)
- Payment Methods: FaucetPay, Litecoin, Cwallet, USDT (ERC20)
- Last Archived Stats: 3,452 members, $718.64 paid
- Referral Pay: Up to 30%
- Status: Domain does not resolve
- Notice: Verdict: offline, a status record. Acashly was a small, script-based GPT and PTC site that appears to have disappeared, with no announcement. We can't review a site that doesn't resolve, so this page records what it said and when. If it returns with verifiable payouts, we'll review it properly.

Acashly (acashly.com) was a get-paid-to and PTC platform: offerwalls and surveys, PTC ads, shortlinks, a faucet, daily tasks and contests, paid out through FaucetPay, Litecoin, Cwallet and USDT with a $1 minimum. The Internet Archive's last copy, from 28 April 2026, showed 3,452 members, 11,636 offers done and $718.64 paid in total, about 21 cents per member. On 2 November 2026 the domain no longer resolves at all. We found no closure notice. If you had a balance there, you can't withdraw it now, so keep your records.

## adBTC

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/adbtc
- Verdict: Recommended, 8/10
- Category: PTC (paid to click)
- Status: Active, scored
- Site Type: Bitcoin PTC / Surf
- Min Payout: 500 Satoshis (~$0.50)
- Payment Methods: FaucetPay, Payeer, BTC
- Available: Worldwide
- Established: 2016
- Our Verdict: Reliable & Established
- Last updated: February 2026

adBTC is a legitimate Bitcoin PTC (Paid-to-Click) site running since 2016. It pays in BTC for viewing ads and auto-surfing, with a low minimum withdrawal. Expect small but reliable earnings, it's one of the more trustworthy PTC sites available. Rating: 8/10.

## ADS by UAP

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/ads-by-uap
- Verdict: Unproven
- Category: PTC (paid to click)
- Status: Unscored or unproven
- Site Type: PTC and traffic network
- Minimum Withdrawal: $0.05
- Payout Channels: FaucetPay, crypto, USD
- Claimed Members: 100,000+
- Claimed Paid Out: $402,000+
- Operator: PassiveTools (no legal entity)

ADS by UAP calls itself 'the premier crypto advertising network'. Members earn by viewing campaigns, advertisers buy traffic, and payouts start at $0.05 through FaucetPay, crypto or USD. It claims 100,000+ active members and over $402,000 paid, and it sits inside PassiveTools, a hub of faucets, virtual-mining games and a rewards comparison page. None of those figures can be checked, no earning rate or advertiser price is shown, and the operator is not named. We found no independent reviews, and ads.uap.company itself didn't load for us. Unproven.

## AiBio.Store

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/aibio
- Verdict: Do Not Deposit
- Category: Offerwalls and GPT sites
- Status: Offline, closed or avoid
- Site Type: Deposit-based "mining game"
- Entry Price: From $1
- Claimed Return: Up to 12% a day
- Deposit Coins: About ten, incl. USDT and BTC
- Referral Levels: 10 levels deep
- Operator: Not named

AiBio.Store is a crypto 'mining game' where you buy virtual machines with a deposit, from $1, and a robot 'mines 24/7'. Its page says a $1 machine earns an estimated up to $0.12 a day and a $100 machine up to $12 a day. That is 12% a day, which pays your money back in about eight days and compounds to over 4,000% a year. Real mining and real ad-funded rewards can't pay that. It also pays referral commissions ten levels deep, doesn't name its operator, and says in the small print that it is 'a game, not an investment'. We recommend you don't deposit. The free robot and free bonuses are the only part worth even looking at.

## Amazon MTurk

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/mturk
- Verdict: Closed, 8.5/10
- Category: Micro-tasks
- Status: Offline, closed or avoid
- Site Type: Micro-Tasks
- Min Payout: $1 (Amazon) / $10 (Bank)
- Payment Methods: Amazon Balance, Bank Transfer (US)
- Available: Primarily US (Limited International)
- Founded: 2005
- Our Verdict: Best Micro-Task Platform
- Notice: MTurk closed on September 30, 2026. Amazon permanently closed Mechanical Turk on September 30, 2026. If you were a worker: you have until October 30, 2026 to confirm your payment method and transfer schedule in the MTurk Worker Portal (Account Settings, then Manage Payment Preferences). Approved HITs are paid on your normal schedule, and HITs still pending approval are auto-approved after 30 days. After October 30, contact MTurk Customer Service for payment changes. Source: MTurk closure FAQs .

Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) is the original micro-task platform, backed by Amazon and running since 2005. It offers the widest variety of HITs (tasks) of any platform, with experienced Turkers earning $6 to $10/hour. The learning curve is steep but the earning ceiling is higher than most micro-earning options. Rating: 8.5/10.

## ARUBLE.NET

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/aruble
- Verdict: Unproven
- Category: Crypto faucets
- Status: Unscored or unproven
- Site Type: Faucet, tasks and ad network
- Faucet Timer: Every 5 minutes
- Reward Unit: "COINS" (value not stated)
- Claimed Users: 1,075,740
- Claimed Paid Out: $500,000+
- Operator: Not named

ARUBLE.NET is a faucet (a claim every five minutes), offers and tasks site that doubles as an ad network: advertisers run PTC, video, banner, popup and shortlink campaigns, and publishers place its ads for a stated 70% revenue share on banners and 50% on popups. Its homepage claims 1,075,740 users and $500,000+ paid out, which is about 46 cents a user. Rewards are in 'COINS' with no stated value, and the page names no payout method, minimum, fee, referral rate or operator. The bookmarked faucet page also returned a 404. Unproven.

Attapoll is a legitimate mobile survey app with a low $3 minimum PayPal payout. Surveys are short and arrive regularly on your phone. Expect $2 to $5/month with occasional higher-paying studies. Rating: 7.5/10, good for a quick passive survey supplement, not a primary earner.

AutoFaucet.org (not the Dutchycorp site of a similar name) is a get-paid-to site that pays crypto for offers, surveys, games, shortlinks, missions and a faucet section, and says it has 500+ tasks. Its headline promises are 'instant cashout', 'various payment methods' and no minimum limit. It doesn't name the payment methods, the coins, the rates, the fees or the operator, and its user and task counters showed only dashes when we looked. ## BeMine

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/bemine
- Verdict: Not a Free Earner
- Category: Mining and deposit schemes
- Status: Unscored or unproven
- Site Type: Cloud mining and GPU rental
- Cost to Start: From $300 (GPU Start)
- Free Option: 3 to 11 day mining trial
- Operator: ART. Research & Development Ltd., Seychelles
- Not Available To: US citizens and companies, Russian citizens and companies
- Referral Pay: 7% level 1, 3% level 2

BeMine is a cloud mining and GPU-rental service, not a micro-earning site. You pay first, from $300 for its GPU contracts, and it credits you a daily return. On its own advertised figures a contract takes between about 1.2 and 3.2 years to pay back, before the electricity fees it doesn't quantify. It is operated by a Seychelles company that names no people, and its Trustpilot page holds only 39 reviews, with withdrawal and payback complaints among them. If you are here to build $1 a day for free, skip it.

## Binance Wallet

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/binance-wallet
- Verdict: Not an Earner
- Category: Wallets, browsers and exchanges
- Status: Unscored or unproven
- Site Type: Web3 wallet (extension, app, web)
- Extension Users: 200,000 (Chrome Web Store)
- Rating: 4.3 from 101 ratings
- Custody Claim: Self-custodial, MPC "keyless"
- Networks: EVM, Solana and TRON in the extension
- Fees: Not stated on the pages we read

Binance Wallet is Binance's Web3 wallet, available as a browser extension, an app and on the web. It's a place to hold and move crypto, not a way to earn: nothing in it pays you for time. Its Chrome Web Store listing describes a self-custodial wallet using MPC (multi-party computation) 'keyless' technology, with 200,000 users, a 4.3 rating from 101 ratings and an update dated 30 October 2026. Binance's own page claims 30M+ wallet users, 30+ networks and $20B+ in monthly volume, but states no fees, and never explains the custody model itself. Several faucet and PTC sites let you cash out to Binance, so you may meet it that way. It's a reasonable, mainstream tool, with the usual cautions about what you approve and where your recovery backup lives.

## Brave Browser

Brave Browser is a legitimate privacy browser that pays you in BAT (Basic Attention Token) just for browsing the web. Earnings are small ($1 to $5/month) but entirely passive, you earn while doing what you'd do anyway. It replaces Chrome or Firefox with no change to your workflow. Rating: 8.8/10.

## BTCClicks

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/btcclicks
- Verdict: Offline
- Category: PTC (paid to click)
- Status: Offline, closed or avoid
- Site Type: Bitcoin PTC (paid to click)
- Status: Offline (Cloudflare 522)
- Last Working Archive Copy: 2 February 2026
- First Error Archive Copy: 17 February 2026
- Announcement: None found
- Operator: Not named
- Notice: Verdict: offline, don't rely on it. BTCClicks has not loaded since mid-February and nothing from the operator explains why. We can't review a site that isn't there, so this page is a status record. If it returns with a verifiable payout, we'll review it properly.

BTCClicks was a Bitcoin paid-to-click site. As of 2 November 2026, btcclicks.com doesn't load: Cloudflare returns error 522, meaning the origin server is timing out. The Internet Archive's records show the site returning normal pages as late as 2 February 2026 and returning that same 522 from 17 February 2026 onward, so it has been down for about nine months. Nothing on the web that we could find announces a shutdown, a payout plan or a return. If you had a balance there, treat it as lost unless the operator reappears, and don't pay for anything claiming to recover it.

BUX.money is one of our new favorite PTC sites. Ultra-low withdrawal thresholds (1-5₽), fast verified payouts, and a modern interface make this a standout platform. We've tested it extensively and can confirm it pays. This should be in everyone's earning rotation. Rating: 8.0/10.

ByteLixir is a legitimate bandwidth-sharing app that pays crypto for sharing your idle internet. It supports fewer devices than competitors like Honeygain and offers crypto-only payouts with variable earnings. Worth running alongside other bandwidth apps but not as a standalone earner.

## Cheddar.tv

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/cheddartv
- Verdict: No Earnings Shown
- Category: Watch to earn
- Status: Offline, closed or avoid
- Site Type: User-video platform
- Earning Model Shown: None
- Last Archived Copy: 6 June 2026
- Sign-Up: Login and sign-up links, SMS verification page
- Legal Pages: Terms, Privacy, DMCA
- Status: Domain does not resolve
- Notice: Verdict: not an earning site on the evidence, and now offline. Cheddar.tv's own pages show a video site with no way to earn, and the domain no longer resolves. If someone told you it pays, we found nothing to support that. Skip the SMS verification and put your time where the terms are published.

Cheddar.tv is not an earning site as far as its public pages show. The Internet Archive's last copy, from 6 June 2026, is a user-video platform ('Say cheese! Create, upload, and share your cheesiest videos') with Home, Bites, Trending and Featured sections, login and sign-up links, and Terms, Privacy and DMCA pages. We found no mention of earnings, rewards, points or payouts anywhere in it. On 2 November 2026 the domain doesn't resolve at all. If you reached an SMS verification page on this domain while looking for paid work, treat it with suspicion: a video site has no reason to pay you, and phone-number checks are a common first step in data-harvesting and fake-reward schemes.

## ClipCoin

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/clipcoin

ClipCoin (clipcoin.pro) is a watch-to-earn site launched in November 2026 by the team behind PayUp.video. You watch YouTube clips of 12 seconds or more on an Android phone and cash out to FaucetPay, TRX, USDT and 8 other methods. It is our current watch-to-earn pick, but it is new and unscored. Use it in your phone's browser, or run the optional auto-view app only on a spare phone.

## CloudResearch Connect

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/cloudresearch-connect
- Verdict: Worth Joining
- Category: Surveys and research
- Status: Unscored or unproven
- Site Type: Paid research studies and surveys
- Minimum Pay Rate: $7.50/hour (from Jan 2025)
- Recommended Rate: $10/hour
- Cash Out: PayPal from $5, bank from $25
- Verification: Stripe Identity (ID check)
- Cost to Join: Free

Connect, run by research-technology company CloudResearch, pays people to join academic and market research studies. Its own figures are good for the category: a $7.50 an hour minimum and a $10 an hour recommended rate for researchers, cash-out by PayPal from $5 or by bank transfer from $25, and a payout center that tracks your balance. The catches are an identity check through Stripe, a quality score that decides how often you're invited, partial-complete studies that can end early with partial pay, and a supply of studies that you can't control. It's a solid second panel next to Prolific, not a daily income.

## CoinAdster

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/coinadster
- Verdict: Use Caution
- Category: Crypto faucets
- Status: Unscored or unproven
- Site Type: Shortlinks, faucet, PTC
- Running Since: 2019 (claimed)
- Payout: FaucetPay or Bitcoin wallet
- Faucet Timer: Every 5 minutes
- Trustpilot: 2.4 from 108 reviews
- Operator: Not named

CoinAdster has paid in Bitcoin for shortlinks, a faucet and PTC ads since 2019, according to its own footer, with withdrawals to FaucetPay or your own Bitcoin wallet. Its Trustpilot profile is the most useful evidence: 2.4 out of 5 from 108 reviews, split between 49% five-star and 36% one-star. Happy reviewers report instant withdrawals as recently as September 2026. Unhappy ones report failed withdrawals, rejected FaucetPay addresses, a hacked account without two-factor authentication, and unanswered support. A long-running site that clearly pays some people, and clearly fails others. Keep balances tiny and withdraw often.

## Cwallet

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/cwallet
- Verdict: Use Caution
- Category: Wallets, browsers and exchanges
- Status: Unscored or unproven
- Site Type: Crypto wallet, exchange and card app
- Company: WEBSEA GLOBAL HOLDING LIMITED (Ontario, Canada address)
- Trustpilot: 2.4 from 108 reviews (62% one-star)
- Highest Leverage: "1001x" perpetual futures
- Claimed Users: 68,547,537 (homepage) vs 37 million (Trustpilot profile)
- Role for Earners: Payout route used by some faucets and PTC sites

Cwallet is a crypto app that mixes a wallet, spot trading, perpetual futures (with '1001x' leverage), a card, earn products and giveaway tools. Many faucet and PTC sites list it as a payout route, which is why readers meet it. It isn't an earning site: you receive coins there, and anything you hold on it is in an account the company controls. Its Trustpilot score is 2.4 from 108 reviews, 62% of them one-star, with the main complaints being frozen accounts, repeated KYC rejections and templated support. Its homepage claims 68,547,537 users, while its Trustpilot description says 37 million, so the figure is unreliable. Use it as a pass-through at most, and don't leave balances on it.

It won't make you rich, but with daily offerwall sessions a $1/day target is achievable. Rating: 8/10.

## FlexCard

FlexCard is not a place to earn. It sells virtual Visa and Mastercard cards that media buyers top up with crypto to pay for Facebook, TikTok and Google ads and for services like ChatGPT. PacketStream is a legitimate bandwidth-sharing app with a $5 minimum PayPal payout. It pays slightly less than EarnApp and Honeygain but is easy to set up and works as a supplementary earner alongside other bandwidth apps. Rating: 7.5/10, worth running alongside Honeygain or EarnApp.

## PayUp.video

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/payup-video
- Verdict: Moved to ClipCoin
- Category: Crypto faucets
- Status: Active, with a status warning
- Platform Type: Video Ads / PTC
- Payout Method: FaucetPay
- Min Payout: Very Low
- Video Length: 10-20 seconds

- Notice: Status update, 10 November 2026: PayUp.video has moved to ClipCoin. PayUp.video is no longer running. Its operators say their hosting provider was hacked and the servers, site backups and databases were damaged, so they have launched a new watch-to-earn project, ClipCoin (clipcoin.pro). PayUp.video is a video ad platform that pays out via FaucetPay for watching short advertisements. Videos are typically 10-20 seconds, the interface is clean, payouts are fast, and there is a solid referral program. Crucially, it is fully automatable with a MacroDroid macro, making it one of the most genuinely passive earners in the stack. PayUp.video is no longer running; its team now runs ClipCoin.

PepeCore (pepecore.one) called itself the 'number one crypto mining platform' and promised to 'earn 200% profits in just 24 hrs' and 'up to 50% daily returns', with 'instant payouts via FaucetPay'. ## Pionex

- Review: https://1dollaperday.com/reviews/pionex
- Verdict: Not an Earner
- Category: Wallets, browsers and exchanges
- Status: Unscored or unproven
- Site Type: Crypto exchange with trading bots
- Cost to Start: Deposit and trade (no free earning)
- Consent Order: NE, NC, OH and SD, $20,000 total penalty
- Admission: None (order says no wrongdoing admitted)
- Trustpilot: 2.5 from 637 reviews
- Its Own Site: Not viewed (security screen)

Pionex is a crypto exchange known for built-in trading bots (grid, DCA and similar). It isn't a micro-earning site: you must deposit and trade, and you can lose money. We couldn't view its own site (it sits behind a Cloudflare security screen), so this review rests on two public records. First, a consent order published by South Dakota's banking regulator, signed by four US states, says an examination found Pionex failed to collect required sender and beneficiary details on transfers over $3,000, and that it had operated in North Carolina and Ohio before it was licensed there. It carries a $20,000 penalty and Pionex admits no wrongdoing. Second, Trustpilot shows a 2.5 score from 637 reviews, split 48% five-star and 40% one-star, with complaints about withdrawals, KYC restrictions and support. Treat it as a trading venue, not an earner.
